newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Six kidnappers die in Manila shootout.
newsitem.headline: Six kidnappers die in Manila shootout.

text.p: Six kidnappers who had abducted two Filipino-Chinese businessmen were killed on Monday in a gun battle with police in a fashionable residential district, officials said.
Chief superintendent Efren Fernandez said the six opened fire on a police car trailing them after an informant had tipped off police that the group planned to abduct a resident of the district.
No policemen were hurt in the shoot-out.
In June, the six kidnappers abducted two local Chinese businessmen whom they released after their families paid a ransom, police said.
Police showed reporters the car they rode in containing bullet holes to show a battle took place and dispel any speculation the six gunmen were summarily executed.
More than 20 police officers, including four generals, face murder charges for the alleged summary execution of 11 suspected robbers in what police said was a shootout on a Manila highway in 1995.

Kidnapping for ransom has become a flourishing industry in the Philippines with criminal gangs collecting 152 million pesos ($5.2 million) in ransom from families of 89 kidnap victims in the first four months of this year, according to statistics compiled by citizens' anti-crime groups.
Widespread belief that soldiers and police protect kidnappers has discouraged Filipinos from reporting incidents to the authorities.
